subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning the full skeleton for a roughly 1.85m knight figure, working through the hip root, spine chain, neck, head, and a jointed great helm with separate jaw plate, then moving to arm and leg chains with basic hand articulation.

For the torso, I'm leaning toward blocky armor built from simple boxes and cylinders attached to bones rather than lofted shapes, keeping it robust. For legs, I'm defining symmetric hip-knee-ankle chains on each side with mirrored x-offsets, parented to the hips joint.

I'm checking leg segment lengths against the hip-to-foot distance so the knee bends slightly forward rather than staying perfectly straight, then layering armor pieces: rod shapes for cuisse and greave along each limb segment, a knee cop, and a sabaton box on the foot.

For the arm chain, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints in an A-pose with the arms angled outward, parenting the chain to the chest/spine joint and naming the three points to form two bone spans plus a wrist tip.

For equipment, I'm putting a large kite shield on the left forearm and a sword in the right hand, working out a natural resting orientation for the blade pointing downward near the thigh.

Actually, let me switch to a point-down sword instead: hilt near the hand with pommel above, guard just below, and the blade hanging down to near the floor beside the leg, offset slightly outward so it doesn't clip. That gives a natural resting-sword pose.

Now I'm working out the wrist joint groove and then the shield geometry, extruding a kite outline positioned in front of the left forearm, considering orientation so it reads correctly from the front viewpoint.

Defining the shield outline points, then considering how the shield arm position relates to the wrist and elbow placement so the arm reads as gripping behind it.

Drafting the griffin emblem as a simplified SVG decal on the shield front, blue field with silver griffin shapes and gold beak and rim accents...

Still building the surcoat geometry...

Adjusting tabard placement so it drapes over the lower chest, leaving the breastplate and gold gorget visible above, then adding a hip belt with a leather box and gold buckle. Now I'm working out torso segmentation along spine joints to size and position the breastplate box correctly.

Writing frustum shapes...

Still refining waist and hip armor...

Now I'm building layered pauldrons from overlapping partial sphere shapes.

Confirming scale and rotation direction for the pauldron domes, then attaching them to the shoulder joint of the arm chain so they follow arm movement. I'm also considering adding gold filigree via a decal projected onto the dome surface for the etched trim effect.

For the gold rim rings, I'll use tori sized to hug each dome's edge with minimal tube thickness, deciding whether to tilt them to match the dome tilt or keep them flat for simplicity -- leaning toward skipping the tilt and relying on the `dir` parameter for a subtle outward lean instead.

For decoration, I'm reconsidering skipping flat decals on curved surfaces in favor of gold studs or small spheres arranged in a ring, though I might still attempt a filigree decal with swirl patterns on the pauldron tops if the surface mapping works out.

I'm now working through the stacked dome positions, figuring out which dome sits on top versus which larger dome below it would actually cover the smaller one visually, to place the decal correctly on the dome that's actually exposed.

Still writing shoulder lames and arm geometry...

For the hand I'll keep it simple with just a fist box and thumb since this arm holds a shield, skipping individual fingers. For the head, I'm building a great helm with a flat-topped cylinder shape, adding an eye slit, breath holes, and a cross-shaped reinforcement band across the front.

Now I'm working out the vertical positioning: splitting the helm into an upper cylinder piece and a separate lower jaw/chin guard piece that can rotate independently, with the head centered around y=1.72 and the overall helm spanning roughly 1.55 to 1.90 before the plume extends it higher.

Checking vertex geometry for the faceted cylinder...

That edge-sticking issue is annoying me, so I'm reconsidering the helm shape entirely -- maybe a boxier frustum is better than a faceted cylinder. Switching to an 8-sided cylinder with a rotated thetaStart so a flat face centers directly at the front seems cleaner, and I'm working out the resulting face width from the angle offset.

Still computing proportions...

Still plotting outline points...

I'm leaning toward smoothing 0 with manually placed points for a faceted, low-poly look, avoiding the risk of smoothing throwing errors when corners cross edges. I'll add a small bevel, set thickness, and plan some darker slabs or grain paint for plume detailing.

Now I'm sketching the cape: a torn crimson shape hanging from the chest joint, defining its ragged outline point by point to get an irregular, tattered bottom edge.

I want it tilted slightly backward so it clears the floor and sits behind the back plate rather than flat against it, adjusting the direction vector so the lower edge drifts further back in z as it descends. Now I'm wondering whether the cape should also drape over the arms.

I'm adding a shoulder mantle piece across the back, small gold clasp spheres at the front neck for the cape fastening, and a subtle gradient tint on the cape fabric going darker toward the hem. For the armor surface I'm layering in a mottled paint effect with a darker steel tone to suggest dents and scratches rather than modeling them as geometry.

I'll add light scratches too, using paint sharing across parts to stay within the color budget, then move on to the leg armor pieces like the cuisse rod from hip to knee.

Still building leg geometry...

For the arms, I'll sweep a tapered chain too, then set up the rig so arms parent from the upper spine with shoulder-elbow-wrist chains built from polyline knots.

I'll skip detailed fingers for simplicity and just give basic hand boxes at the wrist positions, with the left hand positioned to hold a shield strap. For the color palette I'm defining steel, gold, blue, crimson, silver, leather, and dark tones, then planning a mottled blue surcoat paint for texture.

I'm checking the surcoat geometry against the leg and knee placement to make sure the fabric clears the limbs without clipping when the knee bends forward, and verifying the hip joint height lines up properly with the thigh attachment point.

Now I'm setting up the foot target position and sabaton offset, then defining the griffin decal planes for the surcoat front, specifying their size, orientation, texture, and the bone they attach to on the spine.

Next I'm layering the shield decal with a gold rim behind a slightly thicker blue face extrude, working out the exact z-offsets so the rim peeks out around the edges, and positioning the shield relative to the wrist bone.

I need to connect the shield to the arm properly, adding strap geometry so it reads as attached rather than floating. I'll nudge the shield's depth position so its back edge just meets the forearm, settling on a z-center around 0.13 for a snug fit.

Now I'm refining the shield's rim, face, and front plane offsets, then checking against the pauldron's radius to avoid overlap -- shifting the shield outward along x to around 0.7 and verifying its span relative to the wrist position so the proportions still read correctly.

I'm now constructing the sword at the right hand: positioning the grip cylinder, pommel sphere, and guard box relative to the wrist joint, then defining the blade's extruded outline shape with its tapering point coordinates.

Still shaping the great helm...

Now I'm placing small breath holes on the lower jaw plate's front face in a grid pattern, then constructing the lower jaw itself as a tapered bone-colored cylinder positioned beneath the helm, checking it aligns with the neck geometry below.

I'm adding a gorget collar ring around the neck base and another steel gorget piece at the chest, then setting up the jaw joint hierarchy attaching it to the head joint, and working through how the neck chain joints connect back to the spine chain with proper parent references and naming.

Now I'm clarifying the chain naming convention -- a path with N points generates N-1 named spans, so the four-point spine produces three named segments. I'm sweeping a dark mail tube along the neck chain to sit under the gorget, then shaping the breastplate as a tapered box spanning the lower torso, with shoulder width at the pauldrons, and figuring out whether to bind it rigidly to a spine joint or use default skinning.

I'm separately building the waist and hip plates with similar tapered boxes, adding a gold ridge box down the center front to mimic a peascod breastplate, and now working out how the surcoat should drape over it -- adjusting the tabard's top edge so enough of the breastplate still shows rather than being fully hidden.

Writing tabard geometry...

Torso waist box sits narrower than the tabard edges so the mail shows through the gap between tabards. I'm skipping separate faulds and just using a steel box for the hips, then scattering dents across the breastplate's swept surface.

For the dent placement I'm filtering hits so they only land above the tabard line or on steeply angled normals, avoiding spots hidden by cloth. I'll add a few more dents and scratches to the greaves' front-facing surfaces and the pauldron domes, letting them stick across the whole curved area.

Now I'm positioning a gold plume holder near the helm top, sizing the plume itself to arc back and down behind the head so its tail clears the shoulders and cape, bringing the total helm height to about 2.3 units. I'm also considering adding a thinner, darker secondary plume layer on each side for extra feather detail.

Positioning the decal on top of the dome, aiming the direction upward to project the pattern flat against that surface.

I'm deciding against extra gold filigree on the breastplate or gorget, and skipping the cape clasp spheres and chain detail. Now I'm moving to the legs, roughing out sabaton boxes and toe wedges for the sabatons.

Writing geometry parameters...

Still positioning wrist cuffs...

Now I'm starting the actual implementation, importing the builder utilities and setting up the knight's metadata and hip joint as the root of the skeleton.

Building the spine chain and neck/head joints...

Now I'm setting up a loop to generate both legs symmetrically, computing hip and foot positions for left and right sides and feeding them through the limb helper with bend direction hints for the IK solver.

Checking foot and shoulder joint placements against chest and torso proportions, then writing a helper for scattering small dent details across a surface using a seeded random sample with minimum distance spacing.

Still writing pauldron geometry...

Still placing lame geometry...

Now I'm mapping the arm joint chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist, then adding a fist-shaped gauntlet block at the wrist position. Switching to drafting the griffin SVG texture for the crest.

Writing SVG paths...

Still writing filigree strokes... I need to make sure stroke widths stay visible at raster scale, then move on to shield decal placement and part dir/axis options for torus geometry.

Now I'm attaching the cape to the chest bone with a gradient paint, adding a gorget cylinder near the neck, and checking overall height so the plume and sabaton stay within floor bounds. I still need to place the eye slit box and the small breath hole loop on the jaw bone.
